subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: What default recovery policy should OpenClaw apply when an active session transcript is too large or dangerous to open during gateway restart?
rationale: The code fix may quarantine, truncate, skip, reset, or migrate user transcripts, and that affects data preservation, unattended service availability, and operator recovery UX.

options.title: Quarantine and Degrade by Default
options.body: Preserve the oversized transcript for doctor/manual recovery, skip it during startup, and let the gateway continue serving other sessions.

options.title: Auto-Truncate Old History
options.body: Rewrite to a bounded tail or compacted successor automatically, improving continuity but accepting automatic loss of older transcript context.

options.title: Require Operator Repair
options.body: Fail with a clear doctor command and leave all data untouched, preserving state but keeping unattended services down until intervention.

recommendation.title: Quarantine and Degrade by Default
recommendation.body: Preserve the oversized transcript for doctor/manual recovery, skip it during startup, and let the gateway continue serving other sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the current embedded-runner, bootstrap, and internalized agent-runtime architecture where the default recovery policy belongs.
